Included in broader bibliography only; outside empirical retained-harness intervention evidence for this release. A Rust runtime organizes action realization, execution continuity and outcome grounding. The controlled runtime comparison disables memory, evolution and extensions, so it is architectural evidence rather than a demonstrated recursive-improvement loop. Sections 3–5.6.

Included in broader bibliography only; outside empirical retained-harness intervention evidence for this release. Tests whether a first-update winner remains a good choice after another update using separate selection/final tests. The intervention is small-model LoRA training, not harness revision; harm is model-dependent and the no-update control is not compute matched. Sections 3–5.

Included in broader bibliography only; outside empirical retained-harness intervention evidence for this release. Analyzes competitive incentives for self-improvement using a stochastic two-actor game. This is a conceptual safety model, not an empirical demonstration of harness optimization or observed recursive gains. Section 4.

Included in broader bibliography only; outside empirical retained-harness intervention evidence for this release. Collects public repository artifacts associated with coding agents. Configuration and planning files offer a resource for studying harness practice; detection and co-occurrence do not establish causal performance gains or autonomous evolution. Artifact detection and repository classification have distinct validation procedures. Sections IV–V.
